title: Getting started with qteasy
summary: The first hour is an environment, a data channel, one bounded download, and one built-in-strategy backtest, then the tutorial route.
narrative:
The first hour with qteasy has four steps. Install qteasy into a Python environment that can import it; install options, including TA-Lib, are a separate question. Choose a data channel, often a Tushare token, or another supported channel. Download one bounded set of data, for example daily bars of the CSI 300 index for a date range you name. Run one backtest of a built-in strategy on that data. A result report means the one-minute path worked.

The tutorial route after that is: configure the data source, download data, optionally learn the data panel, pick or define a strategy and backtest it, optimize parameters, then read the simulated-live boundary. Ask explains each step. To actually download or backtest, use Plan and confirm. Sample profit figures from the manual are not repeated here.
risk_notes: A download or backtest without an explicit date range is not the first-hour path. Confirm before anything that writes data or recomputes a backtest.
